verdict.summary: LPL Financial is a scaled wealth-management platform whose economics depend on advisor assets, organic net new assets, payout discipline and the yield earned on client cash. Q2 2026 was strong: GAAP net income rose 39% to $379 million, adjusted EPS rose 29% to $5.84, gross profit increased 24% to $1.62 billion and total client assets reached $2.6 trillion. The mix improved as advisory assets grew 46% to $1.5 trillion and reached 60.4% of total assets. The caveat is that organic net new assets were only $23 billion, or 4% annualized, while client cash fell sequentially to $57 billion. Commonwealth integration is the next execution test: management still targets a Q4 2026 conversion and about 90% asset retention. The A- grade reflects durable scale and profitable growth, not a live recommendation. The preserved $362.97/$352.05/$369.98/$379.00 plan is rejected because it pays only 0.64R to TP1 and 1.47R to TP2.
whyBuy: Q2 total client assets reached $2.6T, up 34% YoY; advisory assets rose 46% to $1.5T.
Advisory assets increased to 60.4% of total assets from 55.3%, improving the recurring-fee mix.
Q2 adjusted EPS was a record $5.84, up 29% YoY; GAAP EPS was $4.74, up 39%.
Recruited assets were $25B in Q2 and $89B over the trailing twelve months.
Commonwealth run-rate EBITDA is now estimated at $435M, with approximately 90% asset retention still expected.
whyAvoid: Organic net new assets were $23B, only 4% annualized despite the much larger asset base.
Client cash fell $2B sequentially to $57B and declined to 2.2% of client assets from 2.5% in Q1.
Commonwealth conversion is not complete; the Q4 timetable and 90% retention assumption remain execution risks.
Core G&A is still guided to $2.140B-$2.165B for 2026, including Commonwealth costs.
At $365.50, a simple annualized Q2 adjusted-EPS proxy is about 15.6x; that proxy can overstate normalized earnings if cash yields or markets weaken.

business.overview:
LPL earns primarily from advisory fees and commissions generated on a large advisor-led asset base, plus transaction activity and the spread on client cash. Q2 2026 total client assets were $2.6 trillion, including $1.5 trillion of advisory assets; the shift toward advisory assets makes revenue more recurring but still market-sensitive.

The technology and AI transmission channel is operational, not an AI-product multiple: better advisor workflows, data, compliance and portfolio tools can improve recruiting, asset retention and advisor productivity. The economic proof is recruited assets, organic net new assets, gross profit and controlled core G&A, not the number of AI announcements.

The model breaks if markets reduce fee-bearing assets, clients reallocate cash away from sweep programs, advisor recruiting slows, or Commonwealth conversion causes attrition and cost overruns. Interest-rate changes can also move cash-sweep economics faster than headline client assets and reported growth suggest.
business.moat: LPL's moat is the combination of a $2.6T custody and brokerage platform, advisor recruiting infrastructure, product shelf, compliance stack and transition support. Scale spreads technology and regulatory costs across a large asset base, but advisors and their clients can move: the moat must be measured through retention, recruited assets and organic flows rather than assumed from size.

earnings.beatNote: Q2 2026: GAAP net income was $379M and diluted EPS was $4.74, both up 39% YoY. Non-GAAP adjusted EPS rose 29% to a record $5.84, gross profit rose 24% to $1.618B and adjusted pre-tax income rose 30% to $635M. Total client assets grew 34% to $2.6T, but organic net new assets were 4% annualized and client cash declined $2B sequentially. Management lowered 2026 core G&A guidance to $2.140B-$2.165B and still expects Commonwealth conversion in Q4 with approximately 90% asset retention. The official IR calendar and filed results reviewed through August 28 do not announce the next earnings date, so it remains not confirmed rather than an aggregator estimate.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: LPL ended Q2 with $430M of corporate cash and a 1.91x leverage ratio. It repurchased $309M of stock during the quarter, plans roughly $300M for Q3, and the board added $2.5B to the repurchase authorization on July 23. The current SEC review found ordinary equity compensation and repurchase activity but no reviewed prospectus supplement establishing an ATM. The relevant capital-allocation tension is therefore not micro-cap dilution; it is balancing buybacks and dividends against Commonwealth integration, advisor succession financing and $7.79B of reported debt. LPL does not provide a current fully diluted point-in-time bridge in the reviewed materials, so the dossier does not construct a synthetic total.

filings.finding: The June 2026 Form 10-Q supports the quarter-end balance sheet, ordinary share-based compensation and repurchase activity, and provides the filed basis for evaluating leverage and Commonwealth-related integration commitments.

The 2025 Form 10-K establishes LPL's full-year operating, liquidity and risk baseline, including market-sensitive advisory economics, client-cash exposure, debt obligations and the controls governing equity compensation.
The July 30 Form 8-K furnished Q2 results showing $379 million GAAP net income, $4.74 diluted EPS, $5.84 adjusted EPS and updated 2026 core-G&A and Commonwealth expectations.

contrarianRisks: Commonwealth's expected Q4 conversion and approximately 90% asset retention are targets, not completed outcomes.
Client cash declined to 2.2% of assets; lower sweep balances or lower short rates can pressure cash economics.
Organic net new assets were only 4% annualized in Q2 despite strong recruited assets.
The $2.140B-$2.165B core-G&A outlook includes integration spending and leaves execution risk around operating leverage.
Market declines reduce fee-bearing assets even if advisor count and recruiting remain healthy.

macro.impact: LPLA is a transmission vehicle for equity-market levels, advisor recruiting and client-cash yields. Rising markets lift fee-bearing assets; higher short rates can support sweep economics, while falling rates and cash sorting can compress that benefit. The AI link is indirect through advisor productivity and platform efficiency, not direct semiconductor or software demand.
